title: Boundary pushout products of a cosimplicial arrow resolution
statement:
Use the model-category and homotopy-function-complex conventions of [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and the Reedy structures and relative latching maps of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Let $s:A\to B$ be any arrow of a model category $\mathcal M$. There exist Reedy cofibrant cosimplicial objects $A^\bullet,B^\bullet$, objectwise weak-equivalence augmentations $A^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}A$ and $B^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}B$, and a Reedy cofibration $s^\bullet:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ commuting with these augmentations and $s$. These choices can be made simultaneously for a small set of arrows. For a simplicial set $K$ of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], write $X^\bullet\otimes_\Delta K=\int^{[r]\in\Delta}\coprod_{K_r}X^r$ for the coend (the coproduct modulo the relations induced by simplex operators). For every integer $n\geq0$ define the boundary pushout corner map
$$h_{s,n}: (A^\bullet\otimes_\Delta\Delta^n)\amalg_{A^\bullet\otimes_\Delta\partial\Delta^n}(B^\bullet\otimes_\Delta\partial\Delta^n)\longrightarrow B^\bullet\otimes_\Delta\Delta^n.$$
Every $h_{s,n}$ is an original cofibration with cofibrant domain and codomain. For every originally fibrant $Z$, the simplicial map $H(B^\bullet,Z)\to H(A^\bullet,Z)$, with $H(X^\bullet,Z)_r=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X^r,Z)$, is a Kan fibration representing $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$. It is a trivial Kan fibration if and only if $Z\to1$ lifts against every $h_{s,n}$, and if and only if $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$ is an equivalence. If these conditions hold, then $\operatorname{Map}^h(\operatorname{cod}h_{s,n},Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(\operatorname{dom}h_{s,n},Z)$ is an equivalence for every $n\geq0$. The boundary in dimension zero is empty. The maps $h_{s,n}$ are called horns on $s$ in Hirschhorn's terminology; they use simplex boundaries, not simplicial horn inclusions.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Definition 3.3.8(1), Proposition 3.3.9(1), Lemma 3.3.11(1); Proposition 16.1.22(1), Corollary 16.3.11(1), Corollary 16.5.4(1); Theorem 17.8.4(2)-(3), Proposition 17.8.8(2)-(3) and Proposition 17.8.14(1), printed pp. 60-61, 322, 325-326, 332, 369-374. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Give the walking arrow category $I=(0\to1)$ its direct Reedy structure, with degrees zero and one. By [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], its model category $\mathcal N=\mathcal M^I$ has objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations, and a cofibrant object is exactly an arrow $a:Q_A\to Q_B$ with $Q_A$ cofibrant and $a$ a cofibration. Factor $0\to s$ in this model category as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration. This produces such an $a$ and commuting weak-equivalence augmentations $Q_A\to A$, $Q_B\to B$. Apply [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] in $\mathcal N$ to the cofibrant object $a$, obtaining a frame $a^\bullet$ with degree zero $a$ and augmentation to $\operatorname{const}a$. Write its endpoints as $A^\bullet,B^\bullet$. Latching colimits in $\mathcal N$ are computed at the endpoints. The arrow-model cofibration conditions for $L_na^\bullet\to a^n$ are precisely $L_nA\to A^n$ and $A^n\amalg_{L_nA}L_nB\to B^n$ being cofibrations in $\mathcal M$. Thus $A^\bullet$ is Reedy cofibrant and $s^\bullet$ is a Reedy cofibration; composing the initial cofibration of $A^\bullet$ with it proves $B^\bullet$ Reedy cofibrant. The two endpoint diagrams are frames on $Q_A,Q_B$, and composing their augmentations with the weak equivalences above gives the required resolutions of the original, possibly noncofibrant, $A,B$. Functorial factorization in the Reedy model and the functorial extension construction in the cited Reedy statement allow these choices for every member of a small family, in universes enlarged according to [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Hirschhorn, Proposition 16.1.22(1), printed p. 322; explicit arrow-model/frame construction using the cited existing nodes.

proof.text: The coend $V_X(K)=X^\bullet\otimes_\Delta K$ preserves colimits: its coequalizer formula is built from coproducts, and maps out of it are compatible families of maps from the degrees of $X$. The co-Yoneda relations give $V_X(\Delta^n)=X^n$. A simplex of $\partial\Delta^n$ has image a proper face, so its simplex operators reduce the same coend to the colimit over nonempty proper subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n\}$; this is $L_nX$. Hence $h_{s,n}$ is exactly the relative latching map $A^n\amalg_{L_nA}L_nB\to B^n$, a cofibration by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. The individual $L_nA,L_nB$ are cofibrant: in their finite face-poset diagrams, insert faces in increasing dimension. Inserting a $k$-face attaches $X^k$ along its latching cofibration $L_kX\to X^k$. Starting at the initial object, these finite coproducts and pushouts preserve cofibrations, as seen by assembling componentwise diagonal lifts against any trivial fibration. The same Reedy statement makes $A^n,B^n$ cofibrant. Since $L_nA\to A^n$ is a cofibration, its pushout $L_nB\to A^n\amalg_{L_nA}L_nB$ is one, proving the corner domain cofibrant. For $n=0$ the face poset is empty, both latching objects are initial, and $h_{s,0}=Q_A\to Q_B$.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Definition 3.3.8(1), Proposition 3.3.9(1), printed p. 60; Lemma 16.3.7(1), Proposition 16.3.10(1), Corollary 16.3.11(1), printed pp. 325-326.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] to the colimit-preserving coend functor $V_a:\mathrm{sSet}\to\mathcal N$ of the arrow frame from Step 1. Its boundary maps are cofibrations in $\mathcal N$: at the source endpoint they are $L_nA\to A^n$, and their arrow-relative corner is $h_{s,n}$, both cofibrations by Step 2. Its simplex collapses are objectwise weak equivalences, since the endpoint frames augment to $Q_A,Q_B$ with identity in degree zero. Thus $V_a$ sends every horn inclusion to a trivial cofibration in the arrow model. In particular the relative corner $V_A(\Delta^r)\amalg_{V_A(\Lambda_i^r)}V_B(\Lambda_i^r)\to V_B(\Delta^r)$ is an original trivial cofibration. A horn lifting problem for $H(B^\bullet,Z)\to H(A^\bullet,Z)$ is, by the coend adjunction, exactly a lifting problem from this corner to $Z\to1$. Original fibrancy of $Z$ gives a diagonal by the model lifting axiom. The Kan-Quillen characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] therefore makes this map a Kan fibration. By [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], the endpoint frames represent derived maps from $Q_A,Q_B$ to $Z$. Their augmentations to $A,B$ are weak equivalences, so naturality identifies the resulting map with $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Corollary 16.5.4(1), printed p. 332; relative horn calculation spelled out using the boundary-collapse criterion.

proof.text: Under the coend adjunction, a lift of a boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ into the map $H(B^\bullet,Z)\to H(A^\bullet,Z)$ is exactly a lift against the corner map $h_{s,n}$. The Kan fibration from Step 3 is a trivial Kan fibration exactly when it has the right lifting property against all boundary inclusions, including the empty boundary in dimension zero, by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Therefore it is a trivial Kan fibration if and only if $Z\to1$ lifts against every $h_{s,n}$. The frame mapping identification from [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping] turns this into the equivalence of $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$, and conversely that equivalence of Kan models makes the map a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Corollary 16.3.11(1), Corollary 16.5.4(1), printed pp. 325-326 and 332; Theorem 17.8.4(2)-(3), printed pp. 369-371; Proposition 17.8.8(2)-(3), printed pp. 371-372.

proof.text: Assume the equivalent conditions of Step 4. Naturality of the augmentations gives, for every $k$, a commutative square from $s^k:A^k\to B^k$ to $s:A\to B$ whose endpoint maps are weak equivalences. Therefore $\operatorname{Map}^h(B^k,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A^k,Z)$ is an equivalence. For $n>0$ let $F_n$ be the finite direct poset of nonempty proper subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, ordered by inclusion. Associate to a subset of size $k+1$ the degree $A^k$ or $B^k$, with maps given by the corresponding ordered face inclusions. Their latching maps are exactly $L_kA\to A^k$ and $L_kB\to B^k$, so these are cofibrant diagrams; the relative latching maps of their comparison are $h_{s,k}$. By [lem-coef-finite-reedy-localization], their ordinary colimits $L_nA,L_nB$ are their colimits after localization, including the cocone, and $L_nA\to L_nB$ is a cofibration: for this direct category colimit is left Quillen because its right adjoint, the constant-diagram functor, preserves the objectwise fibrations and trivial fibrations. By the colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], mapping the two localized colimit cocones into $Z$ identifies $\operatorname{Map}^h(L_nB,Z)$ and $\operatorname{Map}^h(L_nA,Z)$ with the limits over $F_n^{\mathrm{op}}$ of the diagrams $\operatorname{Map}^h(B^k,Z)$ and $\operatorname{Map}^h(A^k,Z)$, naturally in the diagrams. The comparison of these diagrams of spaces is an equivalence at every vertex by the first sentences, hence an equivalence of diagrams by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], and so it induces an equivalence of limits: $\operatorname{Map}^h(L_nB,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(L_nA,Z)$ is an equivalence. This also holds for $n=0$, when both objects are initial and both mapping spaces are terminal.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Proposition 17.8.14(1) and proof, printed pp. 373-374 (the latching-object part of the face-poset induction); expressed through the existing finite-Reedy localization and infinity-colimit statements.

proof.text: Put $P_n=A^n\amalg_{L_nA}L_nB$. The span $A^n\leftarrow L_nA\to L_nB$ is Reedy cofibrant: its central object is cofibrant and both outgoing arrows are cofibrations by Step 2 and Step 5. Apply [lem-coef-finite-reedy-localization] to this three-object direct category. It says that $P_n$, with this cocone, is a pushout in the localization. Consequently, by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], $\operatorname{Map}^h(P_n,Z)$ is the homotopy pullback of $\operatorname{Map}^h(A^n,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(L_nA,Z)\leftarrow\operatorname{Map}^h(L_nB,Z)$. Its projection to $\operatorname{Map}^h(A^n,Z)$ is an equivalence because the second leg is, by Step 5. The composite $\operatorname{Map}^h(B^n,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(P_n,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A^n,Z)$ is induced by $s^n$ and is an equivalence by Step 5. Two-out-of-three therefore proves that its first map, induced by $h_{s,n}$, is an equivalence. For $n=0$, $P_0=A^0$ and $h_{s,0}=s^0$, so this is the first sentence of Step 5. This proves the final clause without a simplicial enrichment or a properness assumption.
